topics.title: Cash book vs pass book and the need for a BRS

learn.hook: Your cash book says you have ₹50,000 in the bank. The bank statement says ₹62,000. Nobody is lying. A bank reconciliation statement finds out why.
points: The business keeps the bank column of its cash book; the bank keeps the business's account in its books and sends a copy, the pass book or bank statement.

The two are mirror images: a deposit is debited in the cash book (bank is our asset) but credited in the pass book (the bank owes us). A withdrawal is credited in the cash book and debited in the pass book.

Favourable balance: debit balance in the cash book = credit balance in the pass book (money in the bank). Unfavourable balance (overdraft): credit balance in the cash book = debit balance in the pass book.
A bank reconciliation statement (BRS) is a statement that explains the differences between the two balances on a date and reconciles them.
Importance: it reveals errors in either record, detects frauds and unauthorised payments, highlights delays in clearing cheques, and confirms the correct bank balance.

example.q: Cash book (bank column) shows a debit balance of ₹40,000. What should the pass book show if both records are complete and correct on the same date?
steps: A debit in the cash book means money held in the bank.
For the bank, that money is a liability to the customer, so it shows a credit.
Pass book: credit balance of ₹40,000.
example.answer: A credit balance of ₹40,000 in the pass book.

learn.reallife: A small exporter in Tiruppur reconciles her bank account with the bank's monthly e-statement to catch delays in export receipts and any wrong charges.

topics.title: Timing differences: cheques not presented and not credited

learn.hook: You hand a cheque to your supplier on 30 March. He deposits it on 3 April. For four days your cash book and bank statement disagree, and that's perfectly normal.
points: Cheques issued but not yet presented for payment: the cash book has already reduced the balance; the bank has not. So pass book balance is higher than the cash book balance.
Cheques deposited but not yet collected (credited) by the bank: the cash book has already increased the balance; the bank has not. So pass book balance is lower.
These are timing differences; they disappear when the bank processes the cheques.
Steps in a BRS: start with one balance, add items that make the other balance higher, subtract items that make it lower, and arrive at the other balance.
Starting with the cash book (debit) balance: add cheques issued but not presented; subtract cheques deposited but not credited.

example.q: Cash book balance ₹50,000 (Dr). Cheques issued not presented ₹12,000. Cheques deposited not credited ₹8,000. Find the pass book balance.
steps: Add cheques issued not presented: + ₹12,000 (bank has not paid them yet).
Less cheques deposited not credited: − ₹8,000 (bank has not added them yet).
example.answer: ₹54,000 credit balance as per pass book.

learn.reallife: Cheque Truncation System (CTS) has cut clearing times in India to about a day, but cheques issued on 31 March can still cross into the new financial year.

topics.title: Bank-side items: direct deposits, interest, charges and dishonour

learn.hook: Your bank quietly credits interest, debits SMS charges and pays your insurance premium by standing instruction. You find out only when the statement arrives.
points: Direct deposits by customers into the firm's bank account (e.g. NEFT/UPI receipts): recorded by the bank first, so pass book balance is higher.
Interest allowed and dividends collected by the bank on the firm's behalf: pass book higher.
Bank charges, interest on overdraft, and direct payments made by the bank under standing instructions (insurance premium, EMI): pass book lower.
Cheque deposited and dishonoured: the cash book shows it as deposited, but the bank reverses (debits) it, so pass book is lower.
Starting from the cash book (Dr): add direct deposits, interest and dividends credited; subtract bank charges, direct payments, interest on overdraft and dishonoured cheques.

example.q: Cash book ₹60,000 (Dr). Bank charged ₹500; interest credited ₹1,200; a customer paid ₹7,000 directly; insurance premium ₹3,000 paid by bank. Pass book balance?
steps: Add: interest 1,200 + direct deposit 7,000 = 8,200.
Less: charges 500 + premium 3,000 = 3,500.

learn.reallife: Many Indian households set standing instructions for SIPs and loan EMIs; the debit hits the bank account before anyone writes it in a cash book.

topics.title: Preparing a BRS from the cash book or the pass book balance

learn.hook: Two roads lead to the same destination. You can start a BRS from the cash book or from the pass book; with the right signs, you land on the other balance exactly.
points: Format: Bank Reconciliation Statement as on [date]. Particulars | Plus items (₹) | Minus items (₹). Start with the given balance, list additions and subtractions, and end with the balance as per the other record.

From cash book Dr balance: add cheques issued not presented, direct deposits, interest and dividends credited by bank. Subtract cheques deposited not credited, bank charges, direct payments, dishonoured cheques.

From pass book Cr balance: reverse every sign. Add cheques deposited not credited, bank charges, direct payments, dishonoured cheques; subtract cheques issued not presented, direct deposits, interest credited.
Quick test: for each item ask, 'Which record has it already? Does it make that record's balance bigger or smaller?'

example.q: Pass book ₹90,000 (Cr). Cheques deposited not credited ₹15,000; cheques issued not presented ₹22,000; bank charges ₹600; interest credited ₹1,600. Find the cash book balance.
steps: Add: deposits not credited 15,000 + bank charges 600 = 15,600.
Less: cheques not presented 22,000 + interest 1,600 = 23,600.

learn.reallife: Treasury teams at companies like Tata Steel reconcile dozens of bank accounts every month with software that applies these same plus-and-minus rules.

topics.title: Overdraft BRS and errors in the cash book or pass book

learn.hook: An overdraft is a minus balance. Treat it like a negative number on a number line, apply the usual adjustments, and the BRS works just the same.
points: Overdraft as per cash book = credit balance in the cash book; overdraft as per pass book = debit balance in the pass book.

Starting with overdraft as per cash book: add cheques deposited not credited, bank charges, interest on overdraft, direct payments and dishonoured cheques (they increase the overdraft); subtract cheques issued not presented, direct deposits and interest credited (they reduce it). The result is the overdraft as per pass book.
Shortcut: treat an overdraft as a negative balance and use the normal favourable-balance signs; a negative result is an overdraft.

Errors by the business: e.g. a deposit of ₹5,400 entered as ₹4,500 makes the cash book ₹900 lower, so starting from the cash book add ₹900. Overcasting the receipts side overstates the cash book, so subtract.
Errors by the bank: e.g. the bank wrongly debits another customer's cheque to our account, making the pass book lower; starting from the cash book, subtract it.

example.q: Overdraft as per cash book ₹30,000. Cheques issued not presented ₹8,000; cheques deposited not credited ₹5,000; interest on overdraft ₹1,000 charged by bank. Overdraft as per pass book?
steps: Start: overdraft ₹30,000 (i.e. −30,000).
Cheques issued not presented reduce the overdraft in the bank's books: −30,000 + 8,000 = −22,000.
Cheques not credited and interest increase the overdraft: −22,000 − 5,000 − 1,000 = −28,000.
Overdraft as per pass book = ₹28,000.
example.answer: Overdraft of ₹28,000 as per pass book.

learn.reallife: Small businesses with a cash-credit limit from a cooperative bank often run on overdraft; their BRS starts from a credit balance in the cash book.

Bank errors must be adjusted in the BRS.

quiz.q: Overdraft as per cash book ₹40,000. Cheques issued not presented ₹10,000. Overdraft as per pass book?
quiz.explain: The bank has not yet paid the cheques, so its overdraft is smaller.
steps: Overdraft per pass book = ₹30,000
Answer: ₹30,000

quiz.q: Overdraft as per cash book ₹25,000. Cheques deposited not credited ₹7,000; bank charges ₹500. Overdraft as per pass book?
quiz.explain: Both items mean the bank's overdraft is larger.
steps: Overdraft per pass book = ₹32,500

steps: Cheque received ₹6,300 but entered as ₹3,600.
Cash book is understated by 6,300 − 3,600 = ₹2,700; the bank recorded the right amount.
Starting from the cash book (Dr), add ₹2,700.

quiz.explain: Undercasting payments makes the cash book balance ₹1,000 too high.
steps: Payments side undercast by ₹1,000 means payments look ₹1,000 smaller.
So the cash book balance is ₹1,000 too high.
Starting from the cash book (Dr), subtract ₹1,000.
Answer: Subtract ₹1,000

Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

steps: A: treating an overdraft as negative lets normal BRS signs be used. True.
R: an overdraft is a balance below zero. True.
Because it is just a negative balance, the same rules work, so R explains A.
Both true and R correctly explains A.

topics.title: Amended cash book and BRS from the amended balance

learn.hook: Some differences are the cash book's own fault: unrecorded bank charges, direct deposits, dishonoured cheques. Fix those in the cash book first, then reconcile only what's left.
points: Amended (adjusted) cash book: before preparing the BRS, the cash book is corrected for items the bank has recorded but the firm has not, and for the firm's own errors.

Debit side additions: direct deposits, interest and dividends collected by bank, errors that understated the balance. Credit side additions: bank charges, direct payments, dishonoured cheques, interest on overdraft, errors that overstated the balance.
Items NOT corrected in the cash book: cheques issued not presented, cheques deposited not credited, and errors made by the bank. These remain in the BRS.
BRS from the amended balance contains only these remaining items and ends with the pass book balance.
Advantage: the corrected cash book balance is the true bank balance shown in the balance sheet.

example.q: Cash book ₹40,000 (Dr). Bank charges ₹500; interest credited ₹1,500; cheque dishonoured ₹3,000; unpresented cheques ₹6,000. Find the amended balance and the pass book balance.
steps: BRS from amended balance: add unpresented cheques 6,000.

learn.reallife: Auditors of Indian companies ask for the adjusted bank balance, not the raw cash book figure, before signing off the balance sheet.

options: Bank charges not yet recorded by the firm
An error made by the bank
quiz.explain: Bank charges are a genuine expense the firm has not recorded; the others are timing items or bank errors.
steps: The amended cash book corrects items the firm has missed or recorded wrongly.
Bank charges are a real expense the firm has not yet recorded, so they are corrected.
Timing items and bank errors are not corrected in the cash book; they stay in the BRS.

quiz.q: Cash book ₹55,000 (Dr). Direct deposit ₹8,000 and bank charges ₹400 not recorded. Amended cash book balance?

quiz.q: A dishonoured cheque of ₹5,000 is recorded in the amended cash book on the
quiz.explain: The deposit is reversed: the bank balance falls, so it is credited.
steps: A dishonoured cheque reverses an earlier deposit.
The bank balance falls, so it is entered on the credit side.
So it goes on the credit side of the amended cash book.
Answer: Credit side
quiz.mistake: Thinks dishonour is a receipt

quiz.q: Which item stays in the BRS even after an amended cash book is prepared?

steps: Timing differences are not cash book errors; they clear themselves.

Interest, bank charges and direct payments are corrected in the amended cash book.
Answer: Cheques issued but not yet presented

quiz.q:

Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: After correction, the cash book shows the true bank position for the firm.
steps: A: the amended cash book balance is shown in the balance sheet. True.
R: it includes all bank-recorded items the firm had missed. True.
Including them makes it the true bank balance, so R explains A.
Both true and R correctly explains A.

revise.summary: The amended cash book corrects items the bank recorded but the firm missed, and the firm's own errors. The BRS is then prepared from the amended balance with only timing items and bank errors.
